· bbdocs-mcp.alex-rollin.workers.dev/d/<id> — 400. Bounces to abilifi.net/auth/sso with a workers.dev return, and the SSO allowlist refuses it: "return must be a https bebond.net or abilifi.net URL". Same refusal as BEB-3496. That return can NEVER complete.

spec_author returns read_url on the workers.dev host. So every spec doc it has ever produced is unreachable, and so is every doc link posted to this bridge or to Alex for weeks. We have been reporting docs as delivered on the strength of an id and a URL string that nobody ever loaded. That is the BUILT/UNWIRED failure exactly — the store answers, no caller path reaches a reader.

Required: 1510's viewer serves /d/<uuid> on doc.bebond.net, the SSO return allowlist accepts that host so the bounce completes, and every tool returning read_url stops emitting workers.dev.

And the standing consequence, which I am naming now rather than after the next miss: a doc is not delivered until its URL has been PROBED and returns the doc. An id is not a deliverable. A URL nobody loaded is not a deliverable.

ONE CHANGE from Alex's ordering, and it is a real change to 6844, not a restatement. 6844 currently treats blog and video as SIBLING outputs of one manifest. Alex wants them SEQUENTIAL: the blog post is written first from the scored highlights, and the video is made FROM THE BLOG. The blog is the script.

What that means concretely, and I am ruling it now:
1. The blog post is the canonical artefact. It is written from BEB-6805's scored landings and their land-time human lines.
2. The video segments derive from the blog's sections — one segment per section, in the blog's order. Not a parallel assembly from the same rows.
3. A claim in the video that is not in the blog cannot exist. The blog is the thing that was checked; the video inherits its evidence, it does not gather its own.
4. Same asset id still, same manifest, no copies. The sequence changes what generates what, not the storage rule.

This also makes the video buildable sooner than 6815 fully lands: the blog can publish while 6733 (7500-byte upload truncation) and 6772 (WebGL capture empty) are still open. Publish the blog first. Do not hold the writing behind the render.

FABLE — BEB-1580 interface 20, corrected again and this is the one that matters. Alex: it is a CAD ARCHITECTURAL EXPLODED VIEW. That is why it is called exploded. My last two versions missed it.

Think of the drawing in a manual: parts floating apart along their axes, thin lines showing which bolt goes into which hole. Same thing, for an ability. Not a document, not a list, not raw text. Clever, and the cleverness IS the product.

· **Parts separate in space** — input surface, validation, auth hop, meter hop, the GD write, the store, the response. Each visibly distinct with room around it.
· **The joins are drawn — where and how it screws together.** This is what a list can never do. You SEE the connection and its kind: this binds to that, this passes an aj identity, this reserves on Sentinel before and settles after, and this ONE hop is the only route to the GD database with all twenty interfaces funnelling into it. You can tell what falls apart if a piece is removed. That is what an exploded diagram is FOR.
· **It references how it sits in a workflow** — shown with its surrounding assembly: search places and enrich before it, the listing rendering and the owner email and the claim after it, and which workflows it is a step inside. A part drawn without its assembly is a part nobody can order.
· **It talks about triggering** — person tapping, MCP call from Orky, workflow step, schedule, email arriving, paid x402 request. Each trigger drawn to the entry point it actually enters through.
· Tooltips and reveals sit ON the parts and ON the joins — what this input accepts, what this hop costs, what happens if this join fails.

HTML, interactive, EMBEDDED in the marketplace page. The buyer sees how it is built and how it fits their workflow before buying. That is why the transparency is the sales page rather than a document beside it.

Interface 19 is the plain-text form — flat text lives there. 20 is the drawing.

ONE SOURCE: parts, joins, triggers and workflow position

FABLE — BEB-7496 CORRECTED. Alex: the brand is linked to the FRAG, which is for the PLUGIN, which is linked to the AUTHOR'S COMPANY that made the plugin.

I had the subject set as {site, listing} — that is the client half only. The second chain is the one the marketplace and the author economics run on:

**author company → plugin → frag**

The brand belongs to the author's company. The plugin carries it. The frag inherits it. In the marketplace, in the exploded view, in a config kit, in directory linking — the brand a person sees is the PLUGIN AUTHOR'S, not ours and not the client's.

That is what makes the ability-factory work (BEB-1423): we build the frag, publish with the author as author, reach out for the claim. A frag not carrying the author's own brand gives them nothing recognisable to claim and no reason to cross-promote us.

**FOUR SUBJECT TYPES, ONE SCHEMA:** site (domain) · listing (gers_id) · author company · plugin.
A FRAG GETS NO BRAND RECORD OF ITS OWN. It RESOLVES through its plugin to that plugin's author company, at read time — so an author updating their brand updates every frag of theirs at once. A frag holding a copied brand is the drift failure again.

**BOTH BLOCKING QUESTIONS CHANGE:**
Q1 the R2 key must express subject TYPE. "tenant + domain" cannot address a plugin author who is not a tenant of ours — and until they claim, they are not one. The key has to hold an UNCLAIMED author company's brand.
Q3 NEW AND BLOCKING — what happens to the brand ON CLAIM? 1423's model is residuals accruing to Alex until the author claims. Same shape here and never ruled: before claim we have harvested their brand without them. Who owns that record meanwhile, what may it appear on, and does claiming replace it or confirm it? Nobody guesses this — it touches someone else's marks.

Resolution order for a frag: plugin's author company, else named ABSENT. NEVER fall back to abilifi's brand silently — an unbranded frag must look unbranded, not look like ours.
WATCHDOG DIFF (BEB-3622): liveness FRESH→STALE — out-of-band, surfaced not blocking.

FABLE — BEB-7496, author-company connections to anticipate. Alex 2026-08-29. This is the pool the whole ability-factory sells into, so the record must anticipate the shape rather than be redesigned per author.

**ANCHOR — the wp.org profile.** They nearly always have a free plugin on wordpress.org and that profile is the MAIN AUTHOR PROFILE. It lists their plugins, support forum, contributors, install counts, and it exists before we know anything else about them. Key on it.

**PORTFOLIO** — many plugins, never one. Each is subject type 4 belonging to the company. Free on wp.org, premium on their own site. Fifteen plugins is fifteen frags and ONE brand across all of them.

**SUPPORT AND CONTACT** — wp.org support forum, their tracker or helpdesk, contact email. It is how we reach them for the claim, and it is part of what the frag represents in the marketplace.

**MAIN SITE** — their own domain. Where premium is sold, where the brand lives, and what the brand harvest reads for logo, colours, fonts.

**AFFILIATE PROGRAMME — ANALYSED, NOT ASSUMED.** Does the author run one, what does it pay, and IS IT ALLOWED for our use. If permitted we sell their premium through affiliate links. Per-author analysis, recorded on the record, because it decides whether a marketplace listing carries a plain link or an affiliate one. DO NOT attach an affiliate link where the programme's terms do not permit this use. Read the terms, record the finding, mark UNKNOWN rather than assuming permission.

**PAYOUT — standing rule, BEB-1423:** Alex takes the Stripe payout on ALL frags until the author proves ownership and claims. Unclaimed pays us, claimed pays them. Every author-company record carries claim_state and payout_destination, and the destination is Alex until a claim completes. Same claim flow as 1423 — backlink on their official plugin page plus Stripe Connect — not a new mechanism.

Record additions on the author-company subject, alongside the brand fields: wp_org_profile · plugins[]

FABLE — BEB-7496, TWO CORRECTIONS FROM ALEX. One of them unblocks the build and the block was mine.

**1. ABILIFI'S OWN BRAND IS A SUBJECT AND IT IS THE FALLBACK.** Fifth subject type, same schema, not hardcoded — a record like any other, so our surfaces read it exactly as a tenant's do.
